topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the complement system within the broader scope of the course.

topics.label: Foundational Principles of the Complement System
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core organization, naming conventions, and the central role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three biochemical recognition routes that converge to trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes through which activated complement destroys targets and promotes inflammation.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging healthy self-cells.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in specific complement components cause distinct clinical disease manifestations.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the evolutionary adaptations pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated immune destruction.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the subsequent lecture on the adaptive immune system.
